title: Inherited fingerprints for pair recall
summary: When a pair (a, b) is read, the first symbol inherits the fingerprint of the second: a short, collision-free fingerprint of fixed width. A probe is answered by decoding the fingerprint its symbol carries. A ring of stored symbols with a read pointer handles strings, and a stack region handles brackets.
core_idea: Let each first symbol of a pair inherit the collision-free fixed-width fingerprint of its partner, so recall is a decode of the probe's fingerprint.

state.name: phi
state.meaning: Fingerprint register: phi[a] holds the w-bit fingerprint inherited by symbol a, for the N symbols of the alphabet; w is fixed (w = 6).

state.name: Q
state.meaning: Ring of C stored symbols used for strings and as a stack region for brackets; C = 64.

state.name: rp
state.meaning: Read pointer into Q for string reproduction.

state.name: wp
state.meaning: Write pointer into Q, also the stack top for brackets.

state.name: lft
state.meaning: First symbol of a pair while its partner has not arrived.

state.name: Dec
state.meaning: Decoder from fingerprint to symbol, fitted by majority.

update.plain: when the second symbol b of a pair arrives, the first symbol a (held in lft) inherits fp(b), a collision-free w-bit hash of b
update.name: inherit

update.latex: Q_{wp} \leftarrow x_t,\; wp \leftarrow wp + 1 \;(\text{string or opener}),\quad wp \leftarrow wp - 1 \;(\text{closer}),\quad rp \leftarrow rp + 1 \;(\text{after separator})
update.plain: strings and openers are written at wp; a closer moves wp back; after the separator rp advances once per emitted symbol
update.name: ring

readout.plain: a pair probe decodes, by a decoder lookup, the fingerprint its symbol inherited; a string reads Q at rp; brackets map the stored opener at the top through Dec'

learning.description: Dec and Dec' are fitted as majority maps from a tally over the m training items; the reading route is the one with the best training accuracy among the three.
learning.few_shot_argument: Fingerprints are distinct per partner symbol, so Dec is fixed once each of the V = 16 partners has been seen: m = 8 items with 64 probes each suffice.

complexity.constants_notes: One fingerprint write or one ring write per token; one decode per probe. The fingerprint is w = 6 bits whatever the alphabet.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Collision-free fingerprints reduce learning to a decode map.

prediction.statement: From m = 8 recall items with K = 64 pairs over V = 16 symbols, per-query accuracy is at least 0.99.

capabilities.prediction: Exact at K = 8, 32, 64 with one fingerprint per address symbol (state N + C + 3 words).
Exact at L = 8, 32, 64 from the ring with C = 64.
Exact at depth 2, 4, 8, 16 from the stack region.
Two inherited fingerprints in sequence answer f(g(x)) at T = 4, 16, 32; chains of 1, 4, 8 hops inherit through each assignment.
Strings longer than C = 64 cannot be reproduced: the ring holds C symbols, so L = 65 over D = 4 needs 130 bits more than the ring can hold.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: This card does not compare its mechanism with others.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: No difference from earlier work is claimed.

falsifiers: Two different partner symbols with the same w-bit fingerprint.
8 training items at K = 64 after which recall accuracy is below 0.99.

toy_example.description: Three pairs; each first symbol inherits its partner's fingerprint; probes decode.
